To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the novel TiC counter-electrode, the organic disulfides/thiolates redox couples and the SnS QDs were successfully used for the first time in QDSSC devices, and the catalytic activity of TiC for T(2)(-) and T(-) is better than Pt.
we have fabricated low-cost QDSSCs using the novel TiC counter-electrode and the organic T(2)/ T(-) redox couple, which have reached an efficiency of about 1.0%.
the TiC counter electrode exhibits excellent catalytic activity for both T(2)/ T(-) and I(3)(-) /I(-) redox couples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of low-cost and high-efficiency SnS-based QDSSC using TiC counter electrode, which can be applied to low-cost solar cells.
the use of novel TiC as the counter electrode material for SnS QDSSCs, which is the first report on the use of transition metal carbides as the counter electrode for QDSSCs.
the use of novel TiC counter-electrodes and organic redox couple in QDSSC, which will help to reduce the cost of solar cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TiC/T(2)/T(−) redox couple system is a promising candidate for QDSSCs.
SnS-based QDSSCs with the novel TiC counter and the organic disulphide/thiolate redox couples can be considered as promising candidates to replace Pt-based QDSSC.
the combination of SnS quantum dot and TiC counter electrode can be an alternative approach for low-cost QDSSCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TiC/TiO(2) counter electrode and the T(2)/S(2-)-based QDSSC would be promising for low-cost solar cell applications.
the efficiency of SnS quantum dot solar cell is improved by the use of novel TiC counter-electrodes and the organic redox couples, T(2)/-T(-).

the TiC counter electrode is a good alternative to the expensive Pt counter electrode for QDSSCs, which is based on organic disulfide/monothiolate redox couples, such as T(2)/ T(-) and S(2)-/S(x) (2-) redox couple.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of TiC and organic redox couple can significantly reduce the cost of QDSSCs.
the catalytic activity and selectivity of Ti-based carbide materials are comparable to that of Pt, and that the organic redox couple T(2)/ T(-) is more suitable than I(-)/I (3)(-).
we have demonstrated that SnS QDSSCs can be made with a TiC counter electrode, and that TiC can be a good replacement for Pt as the counter electrode for SnS QDSCs.
